# Nonprincipal ideal generated by a prime and an indeterminate

↑ **Parent:** [Principal ideal domain](principal-ideal-domain.md)

For a [prime number](prime-number-split.md) $p$, the [ideal](ideal.md) $(p,X)$ in the [polynomial ring](polynomial-ring.md) $\mathbb Z[X]$ is proper: the constant coefficient of every member is divisible by $p$. If $(p,X)=(g)$, then $g$ divides the nonzero constant $p$, so the additivity of [polynomial degree](degree-of-a-polynomial.md) over an [integral domain](integral-domain.md) makes $g$ constant. Since $g$ also divides $X$, it must divide its leading coefficient $1$; thus $g=\pm1$. This would make the ideal the whole ring, a contradiction. Therefore $\mathbb Z[X]$ is not a [principal ideal domain](principal-ideal-domain.md), and hence not a [Euclidean domain](euclidean-domain.md).
